reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Both reviewers read every German string of the unit: title and title.canDo, spec.situation, the start (recapDe, Folge title, 9 Folge lines, gist item), the 3 inputs (LS1 and LS2 dialogues, 10 lines each; the LS3 chat text), 6 exam texts (27 lines), the H1 strategy card, 8 redemittel, the Sp1 task (situation, instructions, openingLine, aiRole, cards, 8 hintWords, 6 model turns), the S1 form task (situation text, 5 fields, checklist, model), the 2 check lines, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine and every explanation.de, and the u01 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json and the rule cards rc.praesens and rc.verbposition-2 that the unit shows. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus its options, tiles or audio line only: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 37 authored pool items, 15 reserve, 6 exam items, 9 check items and 4 proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked each V2 and V1 order against accepted[] and against the Aussagesatz/Frage frame. For the generators we traced what the player builds: 2 × dictation.fromInput per LS1/LS2 (4 sources, none with `say`), 3 × lex.glossTyped (all sources productive), 3 × lex.glossMatch, 2 × perception.pairs. Typed answers and the form fields were graded by running src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js itself on candidate answers (results quoted in F04, F05, F16). Non-exam key positions were counted (13 a / 11 b / 11 c over 35 keys; the r4-F03 class does not recur). Exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1: 6 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, [32–53] words, scaffold allowed in a1.1; sp1: monologue, keyword sheet, then spelling and a number, rubric sd1-sp1 with 3 criteria; s1: form_fill, exactly 5 gaps, situation text [36–48]) and against the rubric files speaking/sd1-sp1.json, writing/sd1-s1.json, course-micro(-sp).json, and against the grader (netlify/functions/_shared/rubrics/grade.mjs, speakingV2.mjs) and the ResultCard that shows the score. Word counts were recomputed with the validator's wordCount: h1 texts 46/46/37/34/35/51, S1 situation 36, LS3 chat 112, LS1 and LS2 dialogues 129 each, Folge 85, cliffhanger 23. We ran the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u01 over every German string of the unit (not only inputs and exam texts), and looked up each unknown token's allocation. The grammar ceiling was read against grammar-spine.json (g.verbposition-2 and g.praesens u01; g.imperativ-sie chunk u01; g.possessiv-mein-dein and g.vokalwechsel u03; g.artikel-genus-plural u04; g.praep-dativ chunk u05; g.trennbare-verben u07; g.muessen-duerfen-man A1.2) and against curriculum/a1-1.md §6 U1 and §9 (chunk table, 'Not in A1.1') and BLUEPRINT §2.5 (hinge: sprichst/spricht as a U1 chunk). New-word load was checked against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32, productive share 0.5). Can-dos were read against registries/cando/a1.json and docs/course-v2/registries-notes/cando-a1.md §2; the cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (languages, origins, voices); story continuity against the authored u02 and u03 (Anmeldung bei Herrn Richter; Emre online in İzmir). The u04 exemplar and its four review rounds were read first, and each of their finding classes was checked here (recurrences are named in the findings and in notes). No 360 px walkthrough was run (the walkthrough reviewer's remit).

validator.result: OK (no blocker findings). 40 rules: 32 pass, 0 fail, 3 warn, 5 skipped (ITM-08, CON-06 — facts[] empty —, and the level-scope COV-1/4/5). ALL-02 gives 3 advisories: tt.sms is listed but no text of the unit has that type (F14); cd.a1.verabschieden and cd.a1.person-erfragen are interaction-spoken can-dos proven by an item alone (F02). GRM-04 gives 16 advisories: 12 × bestimmter Artikel („der Ukraine“, „der Türkei“, „der Sprachschule“, „der Kurs“, „der Prüfung“), 2 × unbestimmter Artikel („eine Stadt“), 2 × trennbare Verben („Und jetzt stelle ich Emre vor.“, „Heute stelle ich Arta vor.“); assessed in F09. LEX-02 gives a ratchet of 7 (begrüßen, woher, sich vorstellen recur in 0 later units; Wohnort, Deutschland, Spanisch, Muttersprache in 1) — measured now against the authored u02–u05 and u07–u10 (F10). LEX-05 passes with 34 entries only through its ±10 % tolerance on the 24–32 band (F10).
validator.notes: Three rails let this unit's findings through, and each is named as a proposedRule: EXM-04 forces the full sd1-sp1 profile onto a reduced Sp1 while the grader scores every criterion (F01); ITM-07 forces exact:number onto the level code „A1“, which checkItem then grades digits-only (F05); ITM-01 recognises only fixed promptEn cue shapes, so „Write the city.“ carries the key's restriction alone (F04). The r1-F10 TXT-02 double tolerance is still in scripts/course-v2/rules/TXT-02.mjs l. 23/36 for non-scaffolded blocks; every u01 text meets the raw registry band anyway.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER, 6 MAJOR, 9 MINOR. The unit has a good skeleton: the first-day story is believable and consistent with u02/u03 and the cast bible, the H1 block and the S1 form are exact to sd1.json in size, options, word bands and key balance, every exam task is original, sentence-building items accept every grammatical order, dictation sources carry no `say`, generator sources are productive lemmas, and the non-exam key positions are balanced. What stops exit: (1) the Sprechen Teil 1 task asks only for the introduction but is scored with the full three-criterion sd1-sp1 profile, so a flawless answer is reported as „1 von 3 Punkten (Richtwert)“, and the Prüfungsfokus calls it 'full' (F01, blocker); (2) the saying-goodbye can-do is never performed and asking is proven only by a tile item (F02); (3) the unit's model question for languages is the calque „Was sprichst du? / Was sprechen Sie?“, drilled as a key and printed on the rule card (F03); (4) three typed items reject a correct answer or accept a wrong one — „Deutschland“ for where Olena lives, „Kurs A1“ in the form (while „1“ is graded correct), and the du/Sie key that the unit's own rule card contradicts (F04–F06); (5) a word card on this unit says Emre speaks English, which the chat and the cast bible deny (F07). The minors are mostly the u04 classes recurring at the point where they hurt most — German-only task surfaces above level on the learner's first day (F08), receptive lemmas typed (F10), unlogged plan deviations (F14).

scoreNotes.D: Most lines are correct and simple, and du/Sie is right in every dialogue. It scores 3 because the unit's own model question for languages is a calque on four model surfaces and the rule card (F03), rc.praesens cites du/Sie without quotation marks („du sagen Sie zu Freunden“, F06), and a handful of teacher lines are stilted meta-talk and one explanation has a broken ellipsis (F11).
scoreNotes.N: Productive lines stay within the u01 ceiling, and „aus der Türkei“ / „Sprichst du …?“ are plan chunks. It scores 3 because the learner meets unglossed later-unit grammar and words exactly where they cannot fall back on English — recap, Folge title, the Sp1 situation (10 unknown tokens in 38 words), the S1 checklist, the cliffhanger (F08) — two separable-verb previews in inputs (F09), and 34 new entries against a band of 24–32 and a plan of 26 (F10).
scoreNotes.H: A believable first day (Folge in the corridor, the intro round, pair questions, the evening chat, Emre and Arta online). It scores 3 because cd.a1.verabschieden is only claimed and cd.a1.person-erfragen is proven by a tile item (F02), and the planned D-A-CH greetings, which would have made the scene lively, are missing (F14).
scoreNotes.A: Keys are right, sentence-building orders are complete, explanations name the position. It scores 3 because a correct answer heard in the audio is rejected (F04), the form's Kurs field grades „1“ correct and „Kurs A1“ wrong (F05), and the du/Sie reserve item contradicts the unit's rule card (F06).
scoreNotes.P: H1 and S1 are exact to sd1.json (H1 scaffolded as allowed; text lengths within the raw bands; all three H1 options heard in 4 of 6 items). It scores 2 because the Sp1 result is produced by a scorer on the wrong rubric and the Teil is labelled 'full' (F01); two H1 items test formulas rather than information (F12).
scoreNotes.K: The cast facts (origins, Emre online in İzmir, Arta in Prishtina, Frau Schulz from Leipzig) and the step into u02 are consistent. It scores 3 because the unit's own word card contradicts the chat about Emre's English (F07), and several small breaks remain (a misquote, Priya's Muttersprache missing in the Sp1 model, an unintroduced Herr Richter, Olena siezt a classmate) (F06, F13).
scoreNotes.E: Items show promptEn, instructions are ≤ 90 characters, and every situation step ends with a named win. It scores 3 because the Sp1 screen shows a 38-word German-only situation that a first-unit learner cannot read (SpeakingTaskView renders situationDe and instructionsDe without an English twin) (F08). No 360 px walkthrough was run.

findings.path: steps[4].task (profile sd1-sp1, instructionsDe, situationDe, aiRole.personaDe); spec.lanes.pruefungsfokus[1].length; registries/rubrics/speaking/sd1-sp1.json; netlify/functions/_shared/rubrics/grade.mjs appliesTo (l. 49) / criteriaPlan (l. 98)
findings.quote: situationDe „… Die Prüfung hat danach noch zwei Aufgaben: buchstabieren und eine Zahl sagen. Das üben Sie in Einheit 2.“ · profile sd1-sp1 = criteria vorstellen / buchstabieren / nummer, max 3 · pruefungsfokus { template: sd1.sp1, length: "full" } · aiRole.personaDe „leitet Sprechen Teil 1 wie in der Prüfung …“
findings.problem: The task elicits only the introduction, which is right for unit 1 (the alphabet and the numbers are u02), but it is graded with the full Teil profile. EXM-04 forces profile = the template's rubric, and criteriaPlan() in grade.mjs scores every criterion of the profile; appliesTo() only knows appliesIf 'targets'. The model is therefore asked to score „Ein Wort buchstabieren“ and „Eine Nummer nennen“ on a transcript that contains neither, and ResultCard shows a flawless introduction as „1 von 3 Punkten (Richtwert)“ with two criteria at 0 — for parts the screen has just said come in Einheit 2. That is a scorer on the wrong pass rule. The Prüfungsfokus entry also declares the Teil 'full' although two of its three parts are omitted, so the chip and the syllabus misrepresent the format. And the persona tells the AI to lead Teil 1 „wie in der Prüfung“, which invites it to ask for spelling and a number that u01 has not taught.
findings.fix: Unit: set spec.lanes.pruefungsfokus[1].length to "reduced" (sd1.sp1 scaffoldAllowedIn a1.1) and end aiRole.personaDe with „Nur die Vorstellung: kein Buchstabieren, keine Zahl (das kommt in Einheit 2).“. Rubric/grader owner: let a SpeakingPart declare the criteria it elicits (e.g. `criteria: ["vorstellen"]`, or `appliesIf: "full"` on buchstabieren and nummer, honoured by appliesTo when the part's length is reduced), so the u01 result is out of 1 and says so. The unit cannot exit before one of the two lands; the alternative inside the rails (moving spelling and a number into u01) would pull u02's content forward.
findings.proposedRule: EXM-04: a speaking part graded with a profile whose criteria are separate performances (sd1-sp1 buchstabieren/nummer, per-part criteria) must elicit each of them in instructionsDe or aiRole, or declare the reduced criteria set; a Prüfungsfokus entry whose task omits a part of the Teil has length 'reduced'. Failing fixture: a1.1-u01 LS5 as it stands. The test runs over all registered courses (sd1.json openQuestions already plans spelling/number-only sp1 slots in A1.1 U5/U8, the inverse case).

findings.path: steps[1].input.lines[0..2] (ls2-l01, -l02, -l03); steps[1].pool.items[6] (ls2-p07); steps[3].texts[2].lines[0] (t3-l01); steps[2].microOutput.situationDe; check.proofItems[3].promptDe (q04); explanations ls2-i01, ls3-i02; a1.1/rule-cards.json rc.verbposition-2 table row 4
findings.quote: „Sagen Sie hier „du“: Wie heißt du? Woher kommst du? Was sprichst du?“ · „Ich frage jetzt: Was sprichst du? Sprichst du Englisch?“ · ls2-p07 tiles [sprechen / Sie / was] → „Was sprechen Sie?“ · t3 „Hallo, Maria! Was sprichst du? Englisch?“ · q04 „„Was sprichst du?“ – „Ich ___ Englisch und Deutsch.““ · rc.verbposition-2 „Was | sprechen | Sie?“
findings.problem: „Was sprichst du?“ is a calque of 'What do you speak?'. A German speaker asks „Welche Sprachen sprichst du?“ (or „Sprichst du Englisch?“); on its own „Was sprichst du?“ reads as 'What are you saying?'. The unit makes it the model question of cd.a1.person-erfragen, whose registry text itself says „welche Sprachen sie sprechen“, and its own exam stem h1-03 already uses „Welche Sprache …?“. It is drilled productively as a sentence-building key, repeated in an exam text and a proof stem, and printed on the rule card as the example of a W-question. Unnatural German on a model surface is a MAJOR (§9.4).
findings.fix: Use the plan's chunk „Sprichst du Englisch?“ (a1-1.md §6 U1, feste Wendung) and add „Welche Sprachen sprichst du? / sprechen Sie?“ as a fixed phrase (spine owner: register it as a u01 chunk; it also licenses the h1-03 stem). Keep „Was?“ in the Leitpunkt with a natural question: „Was lernst du hier? – Deutsch.“ ls2-l01 „… Woher kommst du? Welche Sprachen sprichst du?“; ls2-l02 „Hallo, Priya! Sprichst du Englisch?“; ls2-l03 „… Und du, Bilal? Welche Sprachen sprichst du?“; ls2-p07 tiles [lernen / Sie / was / hier] → „Was lernen Sie hier?“; t3 „Hallo, Maria! Sprichst du Englisch?“; q04 „„Sprichst du Englisch?“ – „Ja, ich ___ Englisch und Deutsch.““; ls3-mo „„Und du? Welche Sprachen sprichst du?““. Rule-cards owner: rc.verbposition-2 row „Was | lernen | Sie?“. Add a redemittel for asking about languages (none of rm01–rm08 does).

findings.quote: ls2-i04 promptDe „Olena wohnt jetzt in ___.“ · promptEn 'Where does Olena live now? Write the city.' · accepted [„Leipzig“] · audio ls2-l07 „Jetzt wohne ich hier in Deutschland, in Leipzig.“ · checkItem: „Deutschland“ → WRONG · ls3-i03 accepted [„Prishtina“], checkItem: „Pristina“ → TYPO
findings.problem: The learner hears „Jetzt wohne ich hier in Deutschland, in Leipzig.“ and writes „Olena wohnt jetzt in Deutschland.“ — true, heard, and graded WRONG. Only promptEn ('Write the city') restricts the gap to the city, which ITM-01 forbids as the only cue (u04 r1-F01/F12 class). ls1-i04 („Frau Schulz kommt aus ___.“) and ls3-i03 („Arta wohnt in ___.“; the chat gives „Land: Kosovo. Wohnort: Prishtina.“) have the same shape. ls3-i03 also grades „Pristina“, the usual German spelling of the city (Duden: Priština, Pristina), as a TYPO that has to be retried.
findings.fix: Put the restriction into German, as p05/p06 already do: „Olena wohnt jetzt in ___. (Stadt)“, „Frau Schulz kommt aus ___. (Stadt)“, „Arta wohnt in ___. (Stadt)“ (each ≤ 90 characters); or accept „Deutschland“ in ls2-i04 with acceptedWhy „auch richtig: Olena sagt „in Deutschland, in Leipzig““. Add „Pristina“ to ls3-i03 with acceptedWhy „deutsche Schreibweise der Stadt“.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01: when promptEn restricts the answer class of a typed item („the city“, „the country“, „the name“, „the number“, „a question“), promptDe carries the same restriction („(Stadt)“, „(Land)“, „Name:“ …); a typed gap whose key is a place name heard next to another place name of a different class (Land/Stadt) is an advisory for the solver gate. Failing fixture: ls2-i04. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: f5 { labelDe: „Kurs“, answer: „A1“, accepted: [„A1“, „A 1“], exact: "number" } · situation „Emre lernt online Deutsch, im Kurs A1 von Frau Schulz in Leipzig.“ · checkItem results: „1“ → CORRECT, „eins“ → CORRECT, „Kurs A1“ → WRONG, „Deutschkurs A1“ → WRONG, „A1 online“ → WRONG
findings.problem: ITM-07 requires exact on every answer that contains a digit, so the CEFR code „A1“ was given exact:number. checkNumber then treats the digit as the task and the letters as optional words: a learner who writes „1“ or „eins“ in the Kurs field is graded correct, and a learner who copies the text's own words „Kurs A1“ (or „Deutschkurs A1“, „A1 online“) is graded WRONG with the tag spelling-meaning. The field thus accepts a wrong answer and rejects defensible ones. The gist item carries the same exact:number on a multiple-choice key (harmless there, because choice items bypass it, but it shows the rail's reach).
findings.fix: Set f5 exact to "name" and accepted to [„A1“, „A 1“, „Kurs A1“, „Deutschkurs A1“, „A1 online“]. Tested with checkItem: „A1“, „Kurs A1“, „A1 online“ → CORRECT; „a1“ → TYPO (case); „1“, „eins“, „B1“ → WRONG. Drop exact from the gist MC once ITM-07 allows it.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-07: a level or room code (/\b[ABC][12](\.[12])?\b/, „Raum B 204“) is an identifier, not a number: it takes exact "name", never "number"; choice items need no exact. Failing fixture: a1.1-u01 f5 with exact "number" and accepted without „Kurs A1“. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.path: steps[0].reserve[4] (ls1-r05); steps[0].pool.items[3] (ls1-p04); a1.1/rule-cards.json rc.praesens (shown in steps[0], steps[2])
findings.quote: ls1-r05 „Olena fragt Bilal im Kurs. Was passt?“ → only „Wie heißt du?“ (banks plateau, mehr-ueben, repair) · rc.praesens „… du sagen Sie zu Freunden und in der Familie, Sie zu fremden Erwachsenen und im Amt.“ · ls1-p04 „Ich ___ Olena. Und wer sind Sie? (sein)“
findings.problem: The unit's rule card teaches „Sie zu fremden Erwachsenen“. Olena and Bilal are adult strangers on their first day, so a learner who applies the card answers „Wie heißen Sie?“ and is marked wrong; the key rests on the course convention that only LS2's „Sagen Sie hier „du““ states, and r05 is a reserve item drawn into Plateau, Mehr üben and repair sets where that line is not on screen. The card also misstates the unit's own usage (the learners duzen each other from the Folge on), and ls1-p04 has Olena siezen someone in the same course („Und wer sind Sie?“) — the only place she does. Finally rc.praesens cites the pronouns without quotation marks, so the sentence reads like the agreement error ✗„du sagen“ in the card that teaches agreement (the u04 r3-F02 class), and „zu fremden Erwachsenen“ is an adjective ending on an A1.1 card.
findings.fix: ls1-r05 promptDe „Im Kurs sagen die Teilnehmer „du“. Olena fragt Bilal. Was passt?“ (≤ 90 characters). ls1-p04 „Ich ___ Olena. Und wer bist du? (sein)“. Rule-cards owner: rc.praesens „„du“ sagen Sie zu Freunden, in der Familie und oft im Kurs. „Sie“ sagen Sie zur Kursleiterin, im Amt und im Geschäft.“ (within ruleCardMaxWords 60).
findings.proposedRule: GRM-05: a German form cited in rule-card prose is quoted („du“, „ist“), as ITM-11 is proposed to require for explanations (u04 r3-F02). Failing fixture: rc.praesens as it stands. The test runs over all registered courses.
